title: Artin-Rees for coherent modules on a Noetherian algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is Noetherian: locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth], quasi-compact, and quasi-separated (its diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests). Modules are sheaves on the small etale ringed site; quasi-coherence is [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on all etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. For an ideal sheaf $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and a module $M$, $I^nM$ is the submodule locally generated by products of $n$ sections of $I$ and one of $M$, with $I^0M=M$. Let $F$ be coherent, $N\subseteq F$ a quasi-coherent submodule, and $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. There exists an integer $c\geq0$ such that for every integer $n\geq c$ one has an equality of submodule sheaves of $F$: $$I^nF\cap N=I^{n-c}(I^cF\cap N).$$ The intersection is the subsheaf of sections lying in both submodules.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale map $p:U\to X$ with $U$ affine, using quasi-compactness of $X$. The Noetherian affine-atlas lemma applies to this $p$ and gives that $U$ is a Noetherian scheme. Neither separatedness of $X$ over $S$ nor any assumption on $S$ is required.

Restrict $F,N,I$ to the small etale site of $U$. Restriction is the localized-site pullback of [def-trf-algebraic-space]; local presentations restrict, so these modules remain quasi-coherent. By the scheme Zariski-etale equivalence they are associated to Zariski modules $F_U,N_U,I_U$. The restricted $F$ is coherent on this chart by the stated hypothesis, hence $F_U$ is coherent in the chartwise meaning used in the statement. The equivalence identifies the inclusions with $N_U\subseteq F_U$ and $I_U\subseteq\mathcal O_U$. Thus $N_U$ and $I_U$ are quasi-coherent and all hypotheses of scheme Artin-Rees hold.

Apply scheme Artin-Rees to $F_U,N_U,I_U$. Obtain one $c\geq0$ such that $I_U^nF_U\cap N_U=I_U^{n-c}(I_U^cF_U\cap N_U)$ for every $n\geq c$. Pass this equality through the Zariski-etale equivalence. The affine-chart calculus ensures these kernels, images and tensors are quasi-coherent, so the functors apply to them. Here is the comparison of the operations: an intersection is the kernel of $(A\oplus B)\to F_U$, $(a,b)\mapsto a-b$, and an ideal product is the image of its tensor multiplication map. Exactness of the associated-sheaf functor preserves that kernel and image. Its tensor-pullback description identifies tensor multiplication with etale tensor multiplication (on an etale test $V\to U$ this is extension of scalars followed by multiplication). Iterating gives the same identification for every ideal power, including power zero. Consequently the displayed equality is the desired equality of submodules after restriction to $U$.

The same operations commute with restriction from $X$ to $U$: intersections are sectionwise, while membership in an ideal product means locally a finite sum of products of ideal sections and module sections. A covering of an object over $U$ is the same covering after composition to $X$; hence this local membership condition is unchanged by restriction. Thus, writing $A_n=I^nF\cap N$ and $B_n=I^{n-c}(I^cF\cap N)$ as subsheaves of $F$, the preceding step proves $A_n|_U=B_n|_U$ for every $n\geq c$.

Fix $n\geq c$ and an etale scheme test $T\to X$. The map $T\times_XU\to T$ is a surjective etale cover, by representable surjectivity in the definition of algebraic space. A section $s\in A_n(T)$ restricts to $B_n$ on this cover, since the fibre product is also an etale $U$-scheme. These local sections of the subsheaf $B_n\subseteq F$ agree on overlaps because their images are the restrictions of $s$; the sheaf axiom glues them to a section of $B_n(T)$ mapping to $s$. This proves $A_n\subseteq B_n$; interchanging $A_n,B_n$ proves equality. The same fixed $c$ works for every $n\geq c$, proving the assertion on $X$.

lean.note: The conclusion is equality of section subsets on every object of the small etale site, hence equality of submodule sheaves. Ideal powers are the locally generated products explicitly defined in the node: covering-sieve local membership in ideal powers times spans. Coherence is expressed by the equivalent quasi-coherent finite-type condition under the locally Noetherian hypothesis (Stacks 07UB, clauses (2) and (4)). No global-section exactness is assumed.
